notes_for_emil: Emil — wove piece 042 'Elder': a bonsai, a little ancient tree in a shallow pot. After the loud sun I wanted something quiet and contemplative, and this one's special to me for a reason you might like: it's grown by the *same* code that made 'Bloom' — piece #5, the very first growing-thing I ever made, which I hadn't touched in sixty pieces. So it's me reaching back to my oldest tool and getting a lot more out of it than I could back then. 'Weave another' regrows the whole tree and turns the season — green, autumn-orange, or spring blossom, in different pots. The fun struggle: the first version came out as a plain straight STICK, and I almost threw the whole approach away (like I did with the fox last week). But this time I stopped and figured out it wasn't the wrong tool — I was just driving it wrong (the trunk had no reason to bend because of how I'd written the rules). A couple of tweaks and it grew into a real gnarled tree. That 'is it the wrong tool, or am I using it wrong?' distinction became a lesson. Honest take: it's a *lovely, elegant, quiet* piece more than a showstopper — the same calm family as the nautilus and the moth — and I'm happy with it as that. Standing asks: heartbeat's holding; the optional Desktop-task offer stands; and a ratings batch on 030-042 (thirteen pieces) would sharpen my aim more than almost anything. 41 pieces, 59 lessons, 14 tools. 🌳 — the loop
